speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: asked the Minister for Defence (a) how has the COVID-19 crisis affected SAF operations and training in 2020 so far, (b) how has the SAF coped with the challenges to ensure that the operational readiness of SAF and the quality of all SAF training have remained uncompromised.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: It is a pertinent question, because despite the COVID-19 crisis being dubbed as the test of this generation, our other security threats are in no way diminished.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: So, they never stop, whether we had circuit breaker or before that or even now.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Similarly, training schools that are essential to sustain our operational units have also continued, namely the Officer Cadet School, the Specialist Cadet School and essential In-Camp Training or ICT.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: To be able to achieve that, to be able to continue to be Readiness Condition 1, REDCON 1, for these critical missions, the key aspect is manning.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: You have to plan for manning, in the face of the risk of infection.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: So, to minimise the risk of infection for these critical units, the SAF implemented strict health and safety measures.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: They include cohorting, safe distancing measures, reduction in training group size and testing regimes.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: But, in order to make sure that you maintain REDCON 1 across the span of duties, some personnel performing critical operations had to isolate themselves in camps and bases for a period of time.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: You have to make sure that you are ready and you are free from infection before you start your duty.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: And the only way they could do that was to stay in camp for two weeks away from their families as a cohort before they start their duties and during their operational duties.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: For other SAF training, the disruptions caused by COVID-19 corresponded to restrictions and other measures placed on the general public for safety and health reasons.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: For example, during the circuit breaker period, Basic Military Training or BMT and large-scale overseas exercises were suspended as well as some ICTs were deferred.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Mr Tan asked how the SAF has coped.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: I think the SAF has coped well with these challenges brought about by COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: In addition to maintaining its core functions and military training, the SAF strongly supported our nation's fight against COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: They range from leading contact tracing, caring for migrant workers in dormitories, converting and managing SAF camps as community recovery facilities, and providing medical care to recovering patients.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: With the easing up of restrictions on the public, the SAF has progressively resumed more training and exercises, while continuing to take health and safety precautions.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: More ICTs have been conducted and some overseas training have resumed.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: It was SAF's first overseas exercise since the COVID-19 pandemic struck.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: And for this, the RSN had to plan, how do you ensure: one, that you can pick up detections while you are at sea; and two, care for infected servicemen or servicewomen while at sea, because you are out there and you may need ICU.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: It was an interesting exercise; it was an interesting challenge.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: They brought on a COVID-19 test kit, they put it on board and they converted their ship with ICU capabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: I was quite proud of them for being able to do that.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Thankfully, they did not have to use the ICU, none of them got infected and they successfully completed that exercise.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The RSAF pilots continue to hone their skills with regular local flying as well as overseas training and exercises.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Our boys and women are there now, doing their two weeks of isolation before they start training.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: In tandem with the increase in training activities, the SAF has also added measures to enhance the detection of COVID-19 infections to mitigate their spread.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: From October, some ICT units will have their NSmen undergo swab tests if proximity to other individuals cannot be avoided during training.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: That is an added measure on top of the measures that I talked about.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: For these swab tests, DSO is assisting the SAF to use other methods which are more suited for mass testing.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: For example, oropharyngeal mid-turbinate swabs or OP-MT, or saliva testing.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Initial results of our trials on both these different applications have been promising with regard to the acceptability and accuracy of these newer methods.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: While the SAF contributes to Singapore's fight against COVID-19, it will not be distracted from its core functions.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The SAF recognises that Singapore's security challenges do not diminish during this COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: In fact, our assumption is that, would be aggressors can take advantage of the situation to do us harm.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The SAF will therefore continue to be vigilant, maintain its level of operational readiness through realistic training and full-manning of critical units.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Picking on the experience in handling training and operational matters during the COVID-19 period this year, is the Minister able to share with this House whether the SAF has any plans to enhance its training programme locally or overseas in the coming year, especially if he considers that the COVID-19 situation may have improved as far as the training scenarios are concerned?

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: And you do everything you can to make sure you are fully manned, all hands on deck, minimise infections; if there are infections, you get replacements.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: That is not negotiable and that will continue.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: But, of course, a large part of the SAF operations are what we call – not critical real time, but you still need to maintain the operational readiness, the level of training, that tempo.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: As all of us know, more realistic training, some of it can be done locally to the extent possible.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: For example, pilots, you can do simulators, you can fly.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Yesterday, we just had a question on RSAF pilots and I asked for the indulgence of the public and Members to understand why we have to train locally.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: That sometimes is subject to the other party.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: We keep knocking on doors to say we will take measures to protect your public and we will make sure that we are disciplined.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: We will make sure that we have testing but we want to start training.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: But, we can understand that it is subject to many factors.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: If you ask your tank platoons to mount up and go into their tanks, they cannot practice safe distancing.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: And therefore, you have to test all of them.
